chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

There is no zakat in silver until it reaches two hundred dirhams; when it reaches two hundred dirhams, there is five dirhams in it. If it increases beyond that, the calculation is based on that: for every forty dirhams, one dirham. And there is nothing in the fractional parts. There is no zakat in gold until it reaches twenty mithqals; when it reaches twenty mithqals, there is half a mithqal in it. Then, based on that calculation, if the wealth increases, for every forty dinars, one dinar.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of silver and gold required to pay zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Zurara from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir or Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, establishes the precise nisab and rates for silver and gold, reflecting the early Shia juristic consensus on monetary zakat. It explicitly excludes fractional amounts (kussur) from the calculation, a detail that distinguishes Shia fiqh in the treatment of minor increments below the threshold. The ruling underscores the continuity of prophetic economic principles within the Imami tradition, linking material wealth to spiritual purification.
